t: Minimum Operations to Make a Special Number
o: A number is divisible by 25 iff its last two digits form one of 00, 25, 50, 75 (or the number is 0). Since we may only delete digits, the optimal strategy keeps a suffix ending in one of those pairs: choose positions i < j with (num[i], num[j]) ∈ {(0,0),(2,5),(5,0),(7,5)}; we must delete everything after j (n−1−j digits) and everything strictly between i and j (j−i−1 digits), totaling (n−1−j)+(j−i−1) = n−2−i operations. To minimize operations we want i as small (leftmost) as possible for each valid pair type. Additionally, if the string contains a '0', we can reduce to a single '0' with n−1 deletions; otherwise delete everything (result 0) with n deletions. Verify: "2245047": pair (5,0) at i=3 → 7−2−3 = 2 ✓. "2908305": pair (0,5)? positions of 0: 2,4; 5 at 6 → i=2 gives 7−2−2=3 ✓. "10": no valid pair; has a '0' → 1 ✓.
k: Divisibility by 25 depends only on the last two digits: 00, 25, 50, 75.
Keeping pair at positions i<j costs n−2−i deletions; fall back to n−1 if any '0' exists (keep one 0), else n (delete all).

a.i: Scan all index pairs (i, j), i < j; if num[i]num[j] is one of the four endings, candidate cost n−2−i. Combine with the fallback (n−1 if '0' present else n) and take the minimum.
s: Set base = n−1 if '0' in num else n.
For each i < j with num[i]+num[j] in {00,25,50,75}, candidate = n−2−i.

a.i: For each target ending (a, b), scan from the right: find the rightmost b, then the rightmost a before it; cost = (n−1−j) + (j−i−1). Taking the min over the four endings plus the fallback is O(n) and avoids the double loop.
s: For each (a,b) in {(0,0),(2,5),(5,0),(7,5)}: scan right-to-left for b, then for a left of it; compute cost.
Fallback: n−1 if a '0' exists, else n.

c.python:
class Solution:
    def minimumOperations(self, num: str) -> int:
        n = len(num)
        ans = n - 1 if '0' in num else n
        for a, b in (('0','0'),('2','5'),('5','0'),('7','5')):
            j = num.rfind(b)
            if j == -1: continue
            i = num.rfind(a, 0, j)
            if i == -1: continue
            ans = min(ans, (n - 1 - j) + (j - i - 1))
        return ans

a.t: O(n) — constant number of reverse scans

w: Edge cases drive this problem: "10" → 1 (delete the 1), "5" → 1 (delete all → 0), "25" → 0. The greedy rightmost-pair choice is safe because for a fixed pair type, the rightmost b minimizes trailing deletions and the rightmost a before it minimizes middle deletions independently. Follow-up: generalize to divisibility by other numbers (e.g., 125 needs three-digit endings).
